title: Grouping, Sharing and Repeated Addition
seo_title: Grade 1 Grouping and Sharing Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_code: Grade 1: Repeated addition, grouping and sharing
standard_text: Solve and explain solutions to practical problems that involve equal sharing and grouping with whole numbers up to 20 and with answers that may include remainders; repeated addition.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 1 maths worksheets: sharing equally, equal groups and repeated addition up to 20. 100 questions with pictures and memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Sharing equally means everyone gets the same number.
  • Grouping makes groups of the same size.
  • 3 groups of 4 is 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
  • Check that every group is the same.

Examples

Example

Share 12 sweets between 3 friends

1 each, again and again

Answer: 4 each

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Unequal sharesEvery share must be the same.
Counting groupsCount the items, not the groups.
Adding once3 groups of 4 is 4 + 4 + 4.

items.e: The plates have 4 and 3. They are not all the same, so it is not equal. Equal means every plate has the same number.

items.q: Make the 2 plates equal. How many grapes must move?
items.e: 8 shared between 2 is 4 each. Move 1 grape from the 5 to the 3. Now both have 4. (Moving 2 makes 3 and 5.)
10 shared between 2 is 5 each. Move 1 strawberry from the 6 to the 4. Now both have 5. (Moving 2 makes 4 and 6.)

items.q: Make the 2 plates equal. How many apples must move?
items.e: 8 shared between 2 is 4 each. Move 2 apples from the 6 to the 2. Now both have 4. (Moving 4 makes 2 and 6.)

items.q: There are 3 bags. Each bag has 5 apples. How many apples altogether?
items.e: Count by 5s, one number for each bag: 5, 10, 15. There are 15 apples.
Count by 5s to 15: 5, 10, 15. That is 3 fives, so 3 bags.
Count by 5s to 20: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 4 fives, so 4 learners.

items.q: There are 14 children. They sit 2 at each table. How many tables do they need?
